display.title: Display settings
lang.label: Language
lang.name: English
levels.c00-l01.brief: Press i to start typing. Then type the missing letter: a capital I.
levels.c00-l01.hint1: Vim starts in NORMAL mode, where letters are commands. The i command switches to INSERT mode.
levels.c00-l01.title: Insert mode
levels.c00-l02.brief: The l key (lowercase L) moves the cursor one step right. Move once, press i, type e.
levels.c00-l02.hint1: i inserts text just before the cursor. The cursor must be on the first l of Hllo.
levels.c00-l02.hint2: Press l, then i, then e.
levels.c00-l02.title: Move right
levels.c00-l03.brief: Esc leaves INSERT mode. In NORMAL mode, j moves down one line. Add the first letter of both lines.
levels.c00-l03.hint1: After you type B, press Esc. Without Esc, the j key types the letter j.
levels.c00-l03.hint2: Press i, B, Esc, j, i, L.
levels.c00-l03.title: Back to normal mode
levels.c00-l04.brief: h moves left, j down, k up, l right. Add the two missing letters: y in the first line, o in the last.
levels.c00-l04.hint1: For the first line: k, h, then i and y, then Esc.
levels.c00-l04.hint2: For the last line: j, j, l, l, then i and o.
levels.c00-l04.title: Four directions
levels.c00-l05.brief: Add the missing o, press Esc, then type :wq and press Enter. This saves the file and quits.
levels.c00-l05.hint1: Commands that start with : only work in NORMAL mode. Press Esc first.
levels.c00-l05.hint2: :w saves, :q quits, :wq does both, :q! quits without saving. Here: i, o, Esc, then :wq and Enter.
levels.c00-l05.title: Save and quit
levels.c01-l01.brief: x deletes the character under the cursor. No INSERT mode needed. Delete the two extra letters.
levels.c01-l01.hint1: Move with h, j, k, l until the cursor is on the extra letter, then press x.
levels.c01-l01.hint2: Press l, x, j, l, x.
levels.c01-l01.title: Delete a character
levels.c01-l02.brief: dd deletes the whole line under the cursor: press d two times. Delete the virus line.
levels.c01-l02.hint1: The cursor can be anywhere on the line.
levels.c01-l02.title: Delete a line
levels.c01-l03.brief: a starts typing just after the cursor. A (capital) starts typing at the end of the line. Fix both lines.
levels.c01-l03.hint1: First line: press a, type o, press Esc.
levels.c01-l03.hint2: Second line: press j, then Shift+A, then Space and 0.
levels.c01-l03.title: Append
levels.c01-l04.brief: I (capital i) starts typing before the first character of the line, from anywhere. Add the word let.
levels.c01-l04.hint1: I does not go to column 0: it stops before the first character that is not a space.
levels.c01-l04.hint2: Press Shift+I, then type let and a Space.
levels.c01-l04.title: Insert at the line start
levels.c01-l05.brief: o opens a new line below and starts typing. O (capital) opens one above. Add both lines.
levels.c01-l05.hint1: Press Shift+O, type ready, press Esc.
levels.c01-l05.hint2: Then press j to go back to the set line, press o, type go.
levels.c01-l05.title: Open a line
levels.c01-l06.brief: u undoes the last change. Ctrl+R does it again. Try it: press d, d (wrong line!), press u, then delete the right line.
levels.c01-l06.hint1: u works in NORMAL mode. Press it several times to go further back.
levels.c01-l06.title: Undo
levels.c02-l01.brief: w jumps to the start of the next word, b to the start of the previous one, e to the end of a word. Delete the two extra letters.
levels.c02-l01.hint1: The cursor starts at the end of the line. Press b, b to reach thenn, then e to reach its last letter.
levels.c02-l01.hint2: Press b, b, e, x, then b, b, x.
levels.c02-l01.title: Word by word
levels.c02-l02.brief: $ jumps to the end of the line, 0 to column zero, ^ to the first character that is not a space. Delete the three extra characters.
levels.c02-l02.hint1: First line: $ then x, then ^ then x.
levels.c02-l02.hint2: Second line: press j, then 0, then x.
levels.c02-l02.title: Line ends
levels.c02-l03.brief: W, B and E (capitals) move like w, b and e, but only spaces separate words: dots and signs do not stop them. Delete the ; and the x.
levels.c02-l03.hint1: Shift+E jumps to the end of the first block: the ; sign.
levels.c02-l03.title: Big words
levels.c02-l04.brief: A number before a command repeats it: 4w moves four words, 3x deletes three characters, 3dd deletes three lines.
levels.c02-l04.hint1: Press 4, w to land on the first #. Then 3, x.
levels.c02-l04.hint2: Then press j and 3, d, d.
levels.c02-l04.title: Counts
levels.c03-l01.brief: d is an operator: it deletes what the next motion covers. dw deletes to the start of the next word. Delete one the.
levels.c03-l01.hint1: Put the cursor on the first letter of a the, with w.
levels.c03-l01.title: Delete a word
levels.c03-l02.brief: d$ deletes from the cursor to the end of the line. D (capital) is the short form. Delete everything after red, the space too.
levels.c03-l02.hint1: The cursor must be on the space after red.
levels.c03-l02.hint2: Press Shift+W, e, l, then Shift+D.
levels.c03-l02.title: Delete to the line end
levels.c03-l03.brief: c works like d, then switches to INSERT mode. cw replaces a word. Change slow to fast.
levels.c03-l03.hint1: Go to the word slow with 3, w.
levels.c03-l03.hint2: Press c, w, then type fast.
levels.c03-l03.title: Change a word
levels.c03-l04.brief: yy copies a line. p pastes below the cursor, P (capital) above. dd also copies the line it deletes. Copy the first line, then move save below play.
levels.c03-l04.hint1: Press y, y, then p: the first line is now there two times.
levels.c03-l04.hint2: Press j to reach save, then d, d and p.
levels.c03-l04.title: Copy and paste
levels.c03-l05.brief: The dot key repeats the last change. Delete the first TODO with dw, then repeat it on the other lines.
levels.c03-l05.hint1: After d, w, press j to go down, then the dot key.
levels.c03-l05.hint2: Press d, w, j, dot, j, dot.
levels.c03-l05.title: Repeat
levels.c04-l01.brief: f then a character jumps to the next one on the line. F (capital) jumps back to the previous one. Delete the ? and the !.
levels.c04-l01.hint1: The ? is to the right of the cursor: press f, then ?, then x.
levels.c04-l01.hint2: The ! is to the left: press Shift+F, then !, then x.
levels.c04-l01.title: Find a character
levels.c04-l02.brief: t and T work like f and F, but stop one character before. After d, they delete up to a character and keep it. Delete everything after keep, but not the ) sign.
levels.c04-l02.hint1: Press f and the comma key to reach the first comma.
levels.c04-l02.hint2: Then press d, t, ): it deletes up to the ) sign and keeps it.
levels.c04-l02.title: Up to a character
levels.c04-l03.brief: ; repeats the last f, t, F or T. The comma key repeats it in the other direction. Delete the three - signs.
levels.c04-l03.hint1: Press f, -, then x. The ; key now jumps to the next - sign.
levels.c04-l03.hint2: Press f, -, x, then ;, x, then ;, x.
levels.c04-l03.title: Find again
levels.c04-l04.brief: gg jumps to the first line, G (capital) to the last one. A number before G jumps to that line: 3G goes to line 3. Delete the two TEST lines.
levels.c04-l04.hint1: Press g, g, then d, d: the first TEST line is gone.
levels.c04-l04.hint2: Then press Shift+G, then the dot key. The dot repeats d, d.
levels.c04-l04.title: Jump to a line
levels.c04-l05.brief: % jumps from a bracket to its partner. d% deletes from the cursor to the partner bracket. Delete file(...) and the comma after it.
levels.c04-l05.hint1: Put the cursor on the f of file. % first looks to the right for a bracket.
levels.c04-l05.hint2: Press w, l, then d, %, then x.
levels.c04-l05.title: Matching bracket
levels.c05-l01.brief: A text object is a piece of text around the cursor. iw is the word under the cursor. ciw replaces it, from any letter in it. Change quiet to loud.
levels.c05-l01.hint1: With cw, the cursor must be on the first letter. With ciw, it can be anywhere in the word.
levels.c05-l01.hint2: Press c, i, w, then type loud.
levels.c05-l01.title: Inside a word
levels.c05-l02.brief: aw is the word under the cursor and one space next to it. daw deletes both. Delete the word old.
levels.c05-l02.hint1: diw would leave two spaces. daw takes one of them.
levels.c05-l02.title: A word
levels.c05-l03.brief: i" is the text between two quotes. a" also takes the quotes. On a line, ci" finds the first quotes by itself. Change the text to hello.
levels.c05-l03.hint1: You do not need to move: the cursor only has to be on the same line, before or inside the quotes.
levels.c05-l03.hint2: Press c, i, ", then type hello.
levels.c05-l03.title: Inside quotes
levels.c05-l04.brief: i( is the text between two brackets. a( also takes the brackets. Change the content to right.
levels.c05-l04.hint1: The cursor can be anywhere between the brackets.
levels.c05-l04.hint2: Press c, i, (, then type right.
levels.c05-l04.title: Inside brackets
levels.c05-l05.brief: A paragraph is a group of lines with no empty line in it. ip is the paragraph under the cursor. ap also takes the empty line after it. Delete the draft paragraph.
levels.c05-l05.hint1: The cursor is already in the draft paragraph. dip would leave the empty line.
levels.c05-l05.title: A paragraph
levels.c06-l01.brief: / starts a search: type some text, then press Enter. The cursor jumps to the next place with that text. Delete the word jammed.
levels.c06-l01.hint1: A short search is enough: only jammed has a j.
levels.c06-l01.hint2: Press /, j, Enter, then d, w.
levels.c06-l01.title: Search
levels.c06-l02.brief: n jumps to the next match of the last search. N (capital) jumps to the previous one. Delete the three xx words.
levels.c06-l02.hint1: Press /, x, Enter, then d, w. Then n goes to the next xx.
levels.c06-l02.hint2: Press /, x, Enter, d, w, then n, dot, n, dot.
levels.c06-l02.title: Next match
levels.c06-l03.brief: * searches for the word under the cursor, forward. # does the same, backward. The cursor is on count. Find the line that uses it, and delete that line.
levels.c06-l03.title: Word under the cursor
levels.c06-l04.brief: ? works like /, but searches up, toward the start of the text. Delete the word not.
levels.c06-l04.hint1: Only one word has an n. Search for it.
levels.c06-l04.hint2: Press ?, n, Enter, then d, w.
levels.c06-l04.title: Search backward
levels.c06-l05.brief: gn is the next match of the last search. cgn replaces it, and the dot key repeats that on the following match. Change every temp to heat.
levels.c06-l05.hint1: Press * to search for temp. Then c, g, n, type heat, press Esc.
levels.c06-l05.hint2: Press *, c, g, n, type heat, press Esc, then dot, dot.
levels.c06-l05.title: Change the next match
levels.c07-l01.brief: v starts visual mode. Moves now select text, from the cursor to where you go. d deletes the selection. Delete the draft text and one of the two spaces.
levels.c07-l01.hint1: j moves the end of the selection one line down, in the same column.
levels.c07-l01.title: Visual mode
levels.c07-l02.brief: V (capital) selects whole lines. p over a selection replaces it with what you copied. Replace the last two lines with one copy of the first line.
levels.c07-l02.hint1: Press y, y to copy the first line. Then go to the last line and press Shift+V.
levels.c07-l02.hint2: Press y, y, Shift+G, Shift+V, k, then p.
levels.c07-l02.title: Whole lines
levels.c07-l03.brief: p over a visual selection also works inside a line. Copy alarm_threshold and put it in place of value.
levels.c07-l03.hint1: Press y, i, w to copy the word. Then j: the cursor is on the v of value.
levels.c07-l03.hint2: Press y, i, w, j, then v, e, p.
levels.c07-l03.title: Replace a word
levels.c07-l04.brief: Ctrl+V selects a block: a rectangle of columns over several lines. d deletes the block. Delete the numbers, the dots and the spaces after them.
levels.c07-l04.hint1: Press Ctrl+V, then go to the last line: the block grows down.
levels.c07-l04.hint2: Press Ctrl+V, Shift+G, l, l, then d.
levels.c07-l04.title: Block
levels.c07-l05.brief: In a block, I (capital) types the same text on every line of the block, at its left side. Put - and a space at the start of every line.
levels.c07-l05.hint1: Press Ctrl+V, then Shift+G: the block is the first column of every line.
levels.c07-l05.hint2: Press Ctrl+V, Shift+G, Shift+I, then type - and a space.
levels.c07-l05.title: Type on every line
levels.c08-l01.brief: A register is a place that keeps text. p uses the unnamed register, and every delete or change overwrites it. Register 0 keeps your last yank: "0p puts it. Change ERR and FAIL to status_nominal.
levels.c08-l01.hint1: Press y, i, w on status_nominal. After the first v, e, p, the unnamed register holds ERR.
levels.c08-l01.hint2: Press y, i, w, f, E, v, e, p, then f, F, v, e, ", 0, p.
levels.c08-l01.title: The yank register
levels.c08-l02.brief: Two single quotes jump back to the line you were on before the last jump. G, gg, / and n are jumps. Put the default mode in place of the ? sign.
levels.c08-l02.hint1: Press Shift+G, $, then y, i, w to copy decontamination.
levels.c08-l02.hint2: Press Shift+G, $, y, i, w, then the single quote key twice, $, v, p.
levels.c08-l02.title: Jump back
levels.c08-l03.brief: In insert mode, Ctrl+R then a register puts its text and you keep typing. Ctrl+R then " puts the unnamed register. Add a seal call for crew_quarters.
levels.c08-l03.hint1: Press y, i, ( to copy crew_quarters. Shift+A types at the end of the line.
levels.c08-l03.hint2: Press y, i, (, Shift+A, type ; seal(, press Ctrl+R, ", then type );
levels.c08-l03.title: Paste while typing
levels.c08-l04.brief: cw deletes OLD into the unnamed register, so Ctrl+R then " would put OLD back. Ctrl+R then 0 puts your last yank. Change OLD to seal crew_quarters.
levels.c08-l04.hint1: Press y, i, w to copy crew_quarters, then j, w to reach OLD.
levels.c08-l04.hint2: Press y, i, w, j, w, c, w, type seal and a space, then press Ctrl+R, 0.
levels.c08-l04.title: Paste the yank while typing
levels.c09-l01.brief: q then a letter records a macro in that register, and REC shows below the buffer. Every key you press goes in, until you press q again. @ then the letter plays it. Ctrl+V and : are blocked in this chapter. Change both lines to "name": value,
levels.c09-l01.hint1: Record the first line, then press j before you stop: the macro ends on the next line, ready to play. f, Space reaches the space whatever the length of the name.
levels.c09-l01.hint2: Press q, q, Shift+I, type ", Esc, f, Space, i, type ":, Esc, Shift+A, type a comma, Esc, then j, q, @, q.
levels.c09-l01.title: Record a macro
levels.c09-l02.brief: @@ plays the last macro again, where the cursor is. Record the change on the first alarm and do not move to the next line. Then go to each other alarm and play it. Change every alarm to off, with # and a space before it.
levels.c09-l02.hint1: Record without j: press q, q, w, c, w, type off, Esc, Shift+I, type # and a space, Esc, q.
levels.c09-l02.hint2: Then press 2, j, @, q for the next alarm, and 3, j, @, @ for the last one.
levels.c09-l02.title: Play it again
levels.c09-l03.brief: A count before @ plays the macro that many times: 7@q plays it seven times. It stops early when a key fails, like j on the last line. Put every sector name in brackets.
levels.c09-l03.hint1: Record the first line and end with j: press q, q, Shift+I, type [, Esc, e, a, type ], Esc, j, q.
levels.c09-l03.hint2: Seven lines are left. Press 7, @, q.
levels.c09-l03.title: Count the plays
levels.c09-l04.brief: A macro can end with a search: n jumps to the next match, so each play finds its own line. Change every ERR to RESET, with # and a space before the line.
levels.c09-l04.hint1: First press /, type ERR and press Enter to reach the first ERR. Record from there, and end the macro with n.
levels.c09-l04.hint2: Press q, q, c, w, type RESET, Esc, Shift+I, type # and a space, Esc, n, q. Then press 3, @, q.
levels.c09-l04.title: Macro and search
levels.c10-l01.brief: Ex commands change many lines at once. :%s/old/new/g replaces old with new: % means every line, and g every match in a line, not only the first one. Every key you type on the command line counts, Enter too. The keys ., q and Ctrl+V are blocked in normal mode in this chapter. Change every unit to node.
levels.c10-l01.hint1: Without g, only the first unit of each line changes. Two lines have two of them.
levels.c10-l01.title: Substitute everywhere
levels.c10-l02.brief: A range before s picks the lines: :3,5s changes lines 3 to 5 and leaves the others alone. You can also select the lines with V and j, then press : and Vim types their range for you. Turn on zone b only.
levels.c10-l02.hint1: Zone b is lines 3 to 5. The lights on the other lines stay off.
levels.c10-l02.hint2: Press :, type 3,5s/off/on/ and press Enter. Shorter: off and on differ only by ff and n.
levels.c10-l02.title: Only these lines
levels.c10-l03.brief: The search part of :s is a pattern. \d matches one digit, and * repeats what comes before it, zero times or more. & in the replacement puts back the text that matched. Put every number in brackets.
levels.c10-l03.hint1: \d\d* is one digit, then any number of digits: a whole number. \d* alone also matches nothing at the start of a line. \+ does not work in this terminal.
levels.c10-l03.hint2: Press :, type %s/\d\d*/[&] and press Enter. The last / is not needed. On AZERTY, \ is AltGr+8, [ is AltGr+5 and ] is AltGr+°.
levels.c10-l03.title: Match a pattern
levels.c10-l04.brief: :g/pattern/command runs the command on every line that matches the pattern. :g/DEBUG/d deletes every line with DEBUG in it. :v does the opposite: it runs on the lines that do not match. Remove the debug lines.
levels.c10-l04.hint1: Press :, type g/DEBUG/d and press Enter.
levels.c10-l04.hint2: The pattern only has to match the lines to delete. Only DEBUG lines have a D, so :g/D/d is enough.
levels.c10-l04.title: Global delete
levels.c10-l05.brief: :norm types normal mode keys on every line of the range, from the start of the line. gU is an operator like d or c, and it turns text into capitals. Put the level at the start of each line in capitals.
levels.c10-l05.hint1: gUw changes the text up to the next word. The colon stops w, so only the level changes.
levels.c10-l05.hint2: Press :, type %norm gUw (g, Shift+U, w) and press Enter.
levels.c10-l05.title: Normal on every line
levels.c10-l06.brief: :m moves the line of the cursor below another line: :m0 puts it at the top. :t copies it instead. With :g, each line in turn goes to the top, so the list ends upside down. Reverse the launch list.
levels.c10-l06.hint1: In a pattern, . matches any character, so /./ matches every line that has text.
levels.c10-l06.hint2: Press :, type g/./m0 and press Enter.
levels.c10-l06.title: Turn it over
